purpose: C.9 Example 4 (cumulative annual milestone vouchers): annual spend crosses both tiers, cumulative tier_mode fires both grant_voucher payloads. No caps, no exclusions, no waiver threshold on this card.

assumptions.note: Ticket sizes (ecommerce 1,800, utilities 1,200) are exact multiples of the base rule's 200-unit -- zero floor loss, no rounding_estimated flag expected. syn_miles has no waiver threshold at all, so the annual fee is always charged in full regardless of spend.

_hand_computation: Monthly ecommerce 40,000 @ ticket 1,800: floor(1800/200)=9, 9*4=36pts/ticket -> ea=36/1800=0.02 (= unrounded 4/200, zero floor loss). Monthly reward = 0.02*40,000 = 800 pts.
Monthly utilities 35,000 @ ticket 1,200: floor(1200/200)=6, 6*4=24pts/ticket -> ea=24/1200=0.02 (zero floor loss). Monthly reward = 0.02*35,000 = 700 pts.
Monthly total 1,500 pts x 12 = 18,000 pts/year (uncapped -- this card has no caps).
Annual milestone-eligible spend = 480,000 + 420,000 = 900,000 >= 800,000 -> BOTH tiers cross (cumulative tier_mode): grant_voucher(vch_a) AND grant_voucher(vch_b) both fire.
Each voucher: face_value 10,000 x utilisation 1.0 x friction 1.0 = 10,000. Two vouchers = 20,000 milestone value.

Points valuation at the declared primary route 'transfer': (transfer_ratio 1.0 x partner_point_value 1.0) x friction 0.8 = 0.8/pt (18,000 pts >= min_points 5,000, eligible). GR = 18,000 x 0.8 = 14,400.
No waiver threshold on syn_miles -- fee always charged in full. Steady fee = 10,000 x 1.18 = 11,800. Year-1 fee = (10,000 joining + 10,000 annual) x 1.18 = 23,600.
